description: Owner-directed shared behavioral acceptance for equivalent Windows Rust/Slint/SQLite and WebGUI Python/browser/PostgreSQL workflows. A normative contract, not a data transport or already-wired runtime loader.

application_scope.webgui: Python/browser and PostgreSQL catalog, jobs and local coordination

contract_relationships.webgui_refinements: WEB-LIFE-001..009 remain WebGUI-specific refinements of matching LIFE-001..009 shared outcomes
contract_relationships.media_state: schema/media-state-classification.json remains the authoritative Artist/Album color and status-dot policy
contract_relationships.comp: schema/comp-report-policy.json remains the independent COMP policy
contract_relationships.catalog_authority: Windows SQLite owns designated synchronized Artist/Album/Track fields; PostgreSQL retains its separately owned operational/derived state

enforcement_state.windows_runtime_loader: not implemented by this policy PR
enforcement_state.webgui_runtime_loader: not implemented by this policy PR
enforcement_state.independent_json_protection_gate: not yet extended to this new file; requires separate owner-reviewed change

requirements.title: Current operation ownership
requirements.rule: Use client-native generations, tokens or equivalent ownership to prevent superseded search, selection, preview, report, and queued decisions from committing stale UI state.
acceptance: The newest valid selection or operation wins even when asynchronous responses complete out of order.
A stale result cannot overwrite the current Artist, Album, artwork, report, status, or queue decision.
Safe navigation remains available; only conflicting actions are blocked.

requirements.title: Usable catalog before secondary work
requirements.rule: Publish already indexed/published Artist and Album presentation promptly; defer unrelated thumbnail decoding, remote metadata/provider results, coordination and full candidate inspection.
acceptance: The initial usable list and selected overview do not await unrelated secondary work.
Equivalent direct and related-Artist navigation converge on the correct current identity.
Startup and selection responsiveness are compared against accepted measured baselines, without inventing fixed latency requirements.

requirements.title: Bounded background work
requirements.rule: Bound parallel discovery, thumbnail, polling, probe, search and coordination work; coalesce identical requests and supersede or cancel obsolete work using each client's mechanisms.
acceptance: No overlapping duplicate requests or unbounded polling loops.
Background activity becomes idle or backs off and cannot starve interactive work.
Retries do not manufacture new processing or ownership events.

requirements.title: Durable queue and decision integrity
requirements.rule: Represent eligible discovery, selection, staged, running, review, verification and terminal states according to each client's authoritative queue. Never treat a stale or invalid decision as valid.
acceptance: Queued or staged work has a visible next state, explicit decision, or terminal outcome; it is not indefinitely stranded behind a hidden gate.
Cancelling or changing context reconciles pending UI against authoritative durable work.
A stale or duplicate action cannot skip extra Albums, bypass nonce/token validation where required, or publish an unverified result.

requirements.title: Phase-accurate progress and completion
requirements.rule: Progress belongs to its active operation and reflects observed work; staging/ready, embedding, verification, successful completion, cancellation and failure remain distinct.
acceptance: A late provider, index or coordination message cannot overwrite newer operation status.
Only verified media/artwork outcomes appear completed or GREEN; staging alone never claims embedded completion.
Where available, report current item, processed/total counts and final outcome without blocking the client.

requirements.title: Evidence-preserving visual classification
requirements.rule: Preserve the owner-approved independent Artist NAME, Album NAME, Album CARD dot and COMP-track contracts while switching views or incrementally hydrating details.
acceptance: Selection, focus or transient hydration cannot discard verified indexed evidence and manufacture an unmatched RED.
Genuine incomplete/error evidence and the Red no-match default remain valid; higher-priority Yellow/Purple evidence remains authoritative.
All independently applicable Album status dots and approved frame/banner semantics are retained.

requirements.title: Deterministic search, COMP and thumbnail authority
requirements.rule: Keep Artist search typed to Artists, Album search typed to Albums, and selected COMP/Album decisions pinned through discovery, artwork preparation and verified write, respecting the canonical COMP policy and configured preferred embedded dimensions.
acceptance: No stale lookup reopens a completed discovery phase or replaces an accepted selected result.
Applicable COMP or Album writes derive their embedded square image at the current configured preferred side (1200 px is the default, not a fixed policy).
No non-artwork media metadata mutation; preserve immutable source WebP and the artwork-only verification gate.

requirements.title: Database ownership and validation provenance
requirements.rule: Maintain Windows SQLite authority for designated synchronized Artist/Album/Track fields and PostgreSQL ownership of WebGUI-only jobs, validation, audit and coordination; lifecycle progress or a refresh is not a transfer of authority.
acceptance: No client silently rewrites the other client's protected catalog ownership fields to clear a notice or appear complete.
Revalidation/completion notices derive only from the actual successfully validated work; cancelled, failed and unseen records are not claimed as verified.
This JSON is a behavioral contract only: it is not database synchronization transport, schema migration or a new data owner.

requirements.title: Shared acceptance without identical implementations
requirements.rule: Equivalent supported Windows and WebGUI workflows must meet the same outcome and failure-boundary acceptance criteria while retaining native UI, job/queue, database and cancellation implementations.
acceptance: Focused tests cover applicable normal, delayed, stale, double-click, cancellation, restart/recovery and terminal cases.
Measure and document genuine runtime parity or deviations independently; a green unit test alone does not prove installed parity.
Reuse accepted evidence; do not rerun unrelated real-writer suites for a documentation-only change.
